note: Agent+Theme+Past is the canonical past-tense transitive event frame (buy/purchase/acquire-type verbs).
Agent+Patient+Past is the canonical past-tense causative change-of-state frame (repair/fix/mend-type verbs).
Agent+Recipient+Theme is the classic ditransitive/dative-shift frame (give/teach/lend).
Agent+Theme is the basic transitive core-argument frame, coherent independent of tense or modality.

Location is a droppable adjunct for these permit/forbid/allow verbs whose real co-argument is Theme (already paired with Agent in mn0005 for the same verbs), so Agent+Location omitting Theme reads as an arbitrary corpus subset, not a frame.
Agent+Patient is the canonical transitive/causative frame (repair, cancel, call off), coherent without tense marking.
Experiencer+Location is the stative locative-existential frame (an entity being/waiting/situated at a place), where location is a core complement, not a mere adjunct.
Patient+Past is the canonical unaccusative/anticausative past frame, an undergoer event with no expressed agent.
Theme+Location is the stative containment/inclusion frame (X included in / posted within Y), where location is a required complement of these verbs.
Theme-only is the recognizable requirement/unaccusative frame where no agent is expressed (needs, requires, makes-a-decision-on).
Agent-only is the classic unergative intransitive frame, a sole actor performing a self-contained action (walk, stroll, arrive).
Patient-only is the classic unaccusative/inchoative frame, a sole undergoer with no agent (begins, starts, commences).

Location alone with no participant role drops the core Agent/Theme present in every example (one example is even a nonsensically reversed sentence), reading as incidental adjunct co-occurrence rather than a unit of meaning.
